PC: ABC assessment: ensure open airway, check for adequate chest rise, (recognize tachypnea), assess brachial or femoral pulse and capillary refill time
Request cardiac monitor and pulse ox, check blood pressure and cap refill
Ensure patent IV is in place, ask for additional IV access
Place patient on O2 as first “drug” administered in shock state

Recognize need for IV fluids and type of fluid bolus, amount to be administered, timing of administration (goal directed therapy with continual reassessment of vitals, perfusion, liver size) and method of delivery (push/pull/stopcock, bolus via syringe push rather than fluid on pump)
Recognize lethargy as sign of hypoglycemia and administer D25 (2-5 cc/kg)
SBP: Call for help – learners must request either rapid response team or help from ER staff (who will be tied up in a pediatric arrest in other room)
